# Switchboard

A terminal coding agent where the model is a slot, not a fixed property of the
tool. You configure a ladder of models, cheapest at the bottom. Before each user
turn, the deterministic router chooses the lowest suitable feasible rung.
Repeated tool calls, error spikes, new test failures, and hedging can propose a
move; round, feasibility, and budget gates decide whether it applies. Every
session is an append-only record that can be priced, replayed, and searched.
Free and open source (MIT), for macOS and Linux.

Version 1.2 adds a searchable TUI workbench with revision-aware file and text
search, an exact read-only Git diff that includes untracked files, bounded
turn-scoped review of recorded agent mutations, semantic language-server views,
atomic revision-checked edits and undo, durable continuity capsules, visible
parallel delegate tasks, static side-effect-free CLI help and completion, and
bounded startup extension diagnostics with a retained-detail drill-down. The
line-oriented REPL and headless mode remain deliberately smaller than the TUI.

Commands run without a sandbox by default. Auto mode uses a configured low-cost
reviewer only under active verified confinement; host-direct, shared-loopback,
opaque, sensitive, external, and Windows commands remain human-approved. A
confined explicit full-network request can remain reviewable. Yolo mode runs
ordinary edits and commands host-direct without prompts, while sensitive and
external actions remain gated. Verified Seatbelt or bubblewrap confinement is
available on request.
